name: signTabulate
title: Calculates the number of negative, zero, positive and missing values

origin.description: Calculates the number of negative, zero, positive and missing values in a numeric vector. For double vectors, the number of negative and positive infinite values are also counted.

arguments.name: idxs
arguments.text: A vector indicating subset of elements to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

origin.details: The counts are named "-1", "0", "+1", and "NA". A double vector also has "-Inf" and "+Inf". Infinite values are included in the corresponding sign count as well as in their own count.

translation.description: Calculates the number of negative, zero, positive and missing values in a numeric vector. For double vectors, the number of negative and positive infinite values are also counted.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A numeric vector. A floating-point array is a double vector. An integer array, or a sequence of ints, is an integer vector. A double missing value is NaN. An integer missing value is None or the R integer NA sentinel.

arguments.name: idxs
arguments.text: A 1-based vector of elements to operate over. None selects every element.

translation.details: The result is a one-dimensional integer array ordered "-1", "0", "+1", "NA". A double vector also has "-Inf" and "+Inf". Infinite values are included in the corresponding sign count as well as in their own count. An integer vector has no infinity counts. Index rules from matrixStats validateIndices live in the signtabulate crate. An out-of-bounds or missing subscript counts as a missing value.
translation.value: A one-dimensional int64 array. Doubles have length 6. Integers have length 4.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.signtabulate import signTabulate

x = np.array([-1.0, 0.0, 1.0, np.nan, -np.inf, np.inf])
signTabulate(x)
